" data-portal-copyright= " Ashley Fraser " **28;6934;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1518292 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mary Huang is 54 years old , unmarried with no children and a career that has taken her all over the globe . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When she returned to Ottawa to help care for her aging parents , she started to think about what she wanted for herself as she grew older . Ever the researcher , Huang , who builds complex planning and forecasting systems for large companies , set out to discover a way to &amp;ldquo ; build my own village&amp;rdquo ; and soon found one &amp;mdash ; a cohousing community . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I lived in New York for six months . I definitely saw where people didn&amp;rsquo ; t know their neighbours and it&amp;rsquo ; s pretty sad , &amp;rdquo ; said Huang , one of about a dozen people who form the nucleus of &lt;a href= " http : //Concordecohousing.ca " &gt;Concord ... , an intentional community in the planning stages . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Concorde&amp;rsquo ; s members are seeking not just to share a roof over their heads , but also whatever they choose to share of their lives . You hear the world &amp;ldquo ; potluck&amp;rdquo ; often in the cohousing world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cohousing is considered to be a model of living that can help avert loneliness and social isolation as more Canadians face aging without a partner or children , or with families that live far away . According to Statistics Canada , t &lt;span class= " ILfuVd " &gt;&lt;span class= " e24Kjd " &gt;he number of people living alone has more than doubled between 1981 and 2016 , from 1.7 million to four million . **26;6964;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; York University anthropologist Margaret Critchlow has described cohousing as &amp;ldquo ; a grassroots model of neighbourly mutual support that can help reduce social isolation and promote positive , active aging . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cohousing encourages independence through awareness that we are all interdependent , Critchlow wrote in a 2013 article in the journal Social Science Directory . &amp;ldquo ; In a senior cohousing community , giving and receiving co-care is entirely voluntary . Members may choose to support each other through such activities as doing errands , driving , cooking , or going for a walk with a neighbour . Being good neighbours helps people age well in a community and they have fun doing it ! &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was this idea of voluntary support that resonated with Huang. &amp;ldquo ; I am pretty self-sufficient and can be an introvert at times . At other times I strike up conversations with random strangers and had some very interesting conversations , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; The idea that this type of interaction can be had just outside my door if I wanted really appealed to me. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Margery Street , 69 , worked for more than 40 years a pharmacist . She has a 32-year-old son with a disability . In the last half decade of her working life , Street&amp;rsquo ; s job took her to retirement homes to talk to residents about their medications . The experience was an eye-opener , she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; One woman said she missed her garden . She was so depressed . So what do they do ? They give her anti-depressants . I thought to myself , &amp;lsquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s no bloody way I&amp;rsquo ; m going to live in one of those , ' &amp;rdquo ; said Street , who is also a Concorde member . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m an only child . My son is an only child . I currently rent an apartment . I&amp;rsquo ; m concerned about social isolation . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;6992;TOOLONG ... title= " Mary Huang is one of the founding members of Ottawa 's Concorde , a multi-generational cohousing community still in the planning phases . " alt= " Mary Huang is one of the founding members of Ottawa 's Concorde , a multi-generational cohousing community still in the planning phases . " data-portal-copyright= " Ashley Fraser " **28;7028;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1516040 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Could cohousing be one of the answers to helping people age well together ? Many think so . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lynne Markell , 74 , is one of the nine core members of &lt;a href= " http : //Conviviumcohousing.ca " &gt;Conviv ... , a proposed cohousing community for older adults . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m single . I live alone . I don&amp;rsquo ; t have any children . I wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t call myself lonely , but I realize I could live healthier and better with other people around me , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; We believe in the value of community support . Giving help and getting help back . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; People in cohousing communities have the independence of their own private units , which they usually own and can buy and sell , although some communities have low-cost rental units for those who can&amp;rsquo ; t afford to buy in . Residents share communal space that acts as a focal point for gatherings , usually a large kitchen and dining room . There may be a suite for guests or a caregiver , which opens up the possibility of sharing an in-house caregiver. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Most cohousing is set up under the same legal framework either as condos or co-ops , so the legalities and responsibilities are established . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Critchlow has suggested that building a social portfolio might be as important as building a financial portfolio . Cohousing could be &amp;ldquo ; a made-in-Canada model for ageing , not just in place , but in community , &amp;rdquo ; she wrote . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But so far , both Concorde and Convivium are still in the ideas stage . Neither has land or a design to show prospective members . And this is where cohousing appears to be stuck in many cities in Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ontario&amp;rsquo ; s only completed cohousing community is Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s Terra Firma , which opened in 1997 after 12 families bought and renovated two three-door townhouses on Drummond Street near Saint Paul University . The members later added an infill building between the townhouses which includes a seventh residential unit and common space for hosting events ranging from community meals to dance parties and art classes . The yard behind the units is shared by all and contains a trampoline , treehouse , swing and sitting areas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In a way , we &amp;lsquo ; re not doing anything different than what people with condos do . We just have a different intent , &amp;rdquo ; said Steven Fick , who has been a member in Terra Firma since the beginning . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fick was in his 40s when he bought into Terra Firma . He wasn&amp;rsquo ; t thinking about social networks and their connection to healthy aging at that point , but has since realized how much his community may help him age well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; One of the strongest predictors of longevity is social connection , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the real estate market in central Ottawa has changed in the past 22 years . Like most other cohousing groups across the country , Concorde and Convivium have stumbled on the hard reality of acquiring land , a developer and bridge financing to take the idea from concept to reality , all the while keeping the momentum going and the group cohesive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Convivium started about four years ago as an effort to get a seniors cohousing community at Greystone Village &lt;span class= " st " &gt;on former Oblate lands between Main Street and the Rideau River . &lt;/span&gt; When that didn&amp;rsquo ; t work out , the group started the search for its own land . But raw land in a central location is expensive , and the group would have to self-finance the project through the planning and design process until the members were ready to swap the equity they had in their homes and move into their new units . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s all a matter of timing , &amp;rdquo ; said Convivium member Markell. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The group now wants to buy a small apartment building or perhaps a couple of adjacent buildings to retrofit them . It&amp;rsquo ; s faster than starting with the land , and at least people can look at the buildings and imagine what a retrofit would look like , she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Perth , a cohousing community called &lt;a href= " http : **25;7058;TOOLONG " &gt;Tay Commons&lt;/a&gt; began more than four years ago when a group of friends held a potluck and agreed they didn&amp;rsquo ; t want to end up in long-term care . What they wanted was a sense of community , caring for each other and living in a modest and environmentally-friendly way . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In theory , you can live together more cheaply , &amp;rdquo ; said Tay Commons member Doug Burt , 74. &amp;ldquo ; A lot of cohousing people are independent thinkers . They want control over their own destinies . And privacy . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The group decided it didn&amp;rsquo ; t need a large property and acquired an option on a small plot of land that was once part of a municipal works yard a few blocks from Perth&amp;rsquo ; s historic downtown . They envisioned a three-story apartment block with units ranging from about 850 square feet to about 1,000 square feet and hired an architect . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But Tay Commons is far off from being bricks and mortar . It takes a lot of moving parts to establish a cohousing community and keep it going . One member of the group had a partner who was not sold on the idea . Another was supportive , but didn&amp;rsquo ; t see herself moving in , said Louise McDiarmid , 76 , who is one of Tay Commons&amp;rsquo ; founding members . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The costs ballooned . The original quote to build came in at $3.3 million , which included about $150,000 for the land . But because the space was tight , it had to be designed to allow access for emergency vehicles . The next quote came in at $4.4 million , plus an estimated $300 a month for each unit to cover condo fees . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That put the nail in the coffin , &amp;rdquo ; said McDiarmid&amp;rsquo ; s husband , Don , 82. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Because of the costs of buying land , designing the community and perhaps hiring a consultant to shepherd it through the process , cohousing is usually an option only for the solidly middle-class . &amp;ldquo ; We might be the last generation to be able to do this , &amp;rdquo ; notes Don McDiarmid. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Historically , most attempts to build co-housing don&amp;rsquo ; t work . At the end , they founder on cost , &amp;rdquo ; said Burt . &amp;ldquo ; The first thing you want to do it build a relationship . You want to make sure it will last . If you can&amp;rsquo ; t knit the community together , then it collapses. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cohousing originated in Denmark in 1964 , when architect Jan Gudmand-Hoyer and a group of friends came up with a plan for 12 houses with a common house and swimming pool . They bought land , but the project never got built . Still , the idea attracted attention and two communities were completed in Denmark by 1973 . Cohousing has taken root in the Netherlands , Scandinavia , the U.S. and B.C. But it&amp;rsquo ; s been slow to get off the ground in Ontario . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Typically , cohousing units are modest in size . Huang said 550 square feet would suit her just fine . The Fick family unit in Terra Firma is only about 1,200 square feet . The Ficks have raised three children in it . Their two daughters still live within a block of the community . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s another way to live lightly , &amp;rdquo ; said Steven Fick. &amp;ldquo ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t need to own things , I just need to have access to things . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Louise McDiarmid started thinking about aging after she read Betty Friedan&amp;rsquo ; s 1993 book Fountain of Age , which looked at the longevity boom and what it would mean for society . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I wanted to have control of my own aging . Betty Friedan spoke of it as a new stage of life with its own challenges and joys . You&amp;rsquo ; re not responsible for children anymore , so you&amp;rsquo ; re willing to take on new risks , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; I feel strongly about the need for community , I feel we need to belong to a group of people who value you for who you are . It was an opportunity to belong to something larger than yourself . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While many see cohousing as a seniors concept , it can work any way the members want . The age range among Tay Commons members is about 20 years . Convivium is for older adults . Concorde aims to be multi-generational. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Concorde member Valerie Thacker Smith , 38 , first experienced co-housing when she visited a friend near Ann Arbor , Michigan . The residents shared a massive kitchen and tool room . They took dance courses and barbecued together . Later , Thacker Smith lived in Haiti , where it is common for families to live in enclaves that cluster around a courtyard with an outdoor kitchen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; People are so much better off . It&amp;rsquo ; s not just the emotional benefits . It has financial benefits , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; Co-housing gives people of all ages a chance to be part of a community and contribute . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Concorde members believe it will take at least 25 people to get the project off the ground , just because so many people are unable to commit . They also know that they face a red-hot market for raw land . The group had considered buying a small apartment building and renovating , but these kinds of buildings rarely come up for sale , and when they do they&amp;rsquo ; re snapped up quickly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a Catch-22 . People don&amp;rsquo ; t want to commit until they know where it would be built , &amp;rdquo ; said Thacker Smith . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;7085;TOOLONG ... title= " Members of Concorde , front from left : Valerie Thacker Smith , Margery Street , Mary Huang , Diana Armour , Jane Keeler , and back row from left : Caroline Balderston Parry , Elliot Sherman , Jennifer Craven , and Jake Morrison of Concorde cohousing Saturday November 30 , 2019 . Part of the reason for the success on the west coast is that there&amp;rsquo ; s a financial institution willing to advance money until projects are completed , said Street . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; No one has really stepped up in Ontario , &amp;rdquo ; said Huang. &amp;ldquo ; You need a bank or financial institution that understands the concept . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Legally , cohousing takes a lot of attention to detail , especially the what-ifs as members age . What if a member develops dementia ? What if someone remarries and the new spouse doesn&amp;rsquo ; t subscribe to the philosophy ? What about adult children who return to the nest ? Some communities have legal wording that gives the surviving members the first right of refusal if a unit is sold so the philosophy can remain intact . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; MacDiarmid sees herself losing freedom as she ages . Already she doesn&amp;rsquo ; t drive at night . The members of Tay Commons don&amp;rsquo ; t plan to be personal support workers for each other , but they would like to share resources , such as driving for groceries . They have pledged to remain a community , even without a common roof over their heads . Some already live within walking distance of each other , and others may join them as houses in the neighbourhood come up for sale . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; How do you maintain the philosophy of cohousing without a house ? The challenge for aging seniors is how to develop community without an actual building , &amp;rdquo ; said Burt . &amp;ldquo ; There is a desire , even if we don&amp;rsquo ; t have a house , to be as close as possible . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;7151;TOOLONG ... title= " Steven Fick in front of his home in Terra Frima . But so far , none have left , said Fick. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We will deal with that when it happens . People want to age here . That might mean needing help with care or meals . It&amp;rsquo ; s a creative process , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; I think part of the attraction is that Terra Firma is like an extended family . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;7217;TOOLONG ... title= " Steven Fick and his neighbour Suzanne talk in their back yard in Ottawa Tuesday Dec 3 , 2019 . " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;7253;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1518295 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Other intentional communities may have a shared religion , a charismatic leader or a utopian philosophy , said Fick. &amp;ldquo ; Cohousing is more down-to-earth and practical . It&amp;rsquo ; s just people trying to figure out how to live closer . For me , it&amp;rsquo ; s not about utopia . It&amp;rsquo ; s about making it as good as it can be under the circumstances . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The members of Convivium are regrouping and plan to have a refined vision within the next few months , said Markell. &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re guinea pigs and we&amp;rsquo ; re choosing it . With some luck , I think we&amp;rsquo ; ll be able to show what&amp;rsquo ; s possible . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Concorde is still looking for more members &amp;mdash ; and land . &amp;ldquo ; We need more members to help do the work since it&amp;rsquo ; s not a simple and easy process , &amp;rdquo ; said Huang. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I know how much richer my life is , &amp;rdquo ; said Fick of his life in Terra Firma. &amp;ldquo ; I have a life that is worth living and I see my life as significant to other people . It&amp;rsquo ; s important to get that reinforcement from people . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;7562;TOOLONG ... title= " Health issues like diabetes and depression and being a caregiver to his ailing father , Ken Roberts , 56 , found himself not only alone , but lonely , which can have detrimental health effects . " alt= " Health issues like diabetes and depression and being a caregiver to his ailing father , Ken Roberts , 56 , found himself not only alone , but lonely , which can have detrimental health effects . " data-portal-copyright= " JULIE OLIVER " **28;7598;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1518197 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the space of a few short years , loneliness has gone from a subject for poets and songwriters to a public health conundrum to be solved &amp;mdash ; not just to promote individual happiness , but as a potential money-saver for the health-care system . Some studies have linked chronic loneliness to the risk of early death , coronary heart disease , stroke , cognitive decline and dementia . People who are lonely are more prone to depression . Loneliness and a lack of social interaction are predictive of suicide among older people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2015 , researchers at the University of Manitoba&amp;rsquo ; s Centre on Aging reported that among people 45-plus who were hospitalized , being lonely was associated with a higher likelihood of returning to hospital . Being more socially isolated was associated with a higher likelihood of remaining in hospital for longer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All this evidence is piling up at the same time that shifting demographics point to a solitary future for many Canadians . The 2016 census found that , for the first time in recorded Canadian history , one-person households are the most common household type in the country . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As time passes , the reasons for living alone are also changing . In 2016 , about 22 per cent of those living alone were widowed , down from 33 per cent in 1981 . But 32 per cent of those living alone were separated or divorced , nearly triple the rate in 1981. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The whole issue of aging alone is a huge issue for Canada for a number of reasons , &amp;rdquo ; said Nora Spinks , CEO of the Vanier Institute of the Family . &amp;ldquo ; You have densely-populated urban environments , where you can be alone in a crowd . There are suburban environments where lack of transportation can lead to social isolation . And then there are the distances for people in rural areas and the north . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Former U.S. surgeon general Vivek Murthy has called loneliness a &amp;ldquo ; growing health epidemic . &amp;rdquo ; It has been estimated that socially isolated seniors in the U.S. face a 29 per cent greater risk of death &amp;mdash ; and they cost $134 more a month in Medicare spending . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Being disconnected is just as dangerous to good health as smoking 15 cigarettes a day , and is more predictive of early death than the effects of air pollution or being a couch potato , according to oft-cited research by Julianne Holt-Lunstad of Brigham Young University . Another study of 5,100 Americans and their social contacts published in 2008 suggested that loneliness is contagious . When one person feels lonely , it can spread to others in the network . Over time , every additional day of loneliness per week led to about an extra day of loneliness per month for those in the social network . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All of this has called for a response from policy-makers . The United Kingdom has a minister of loneliness , a national strategy , a Campaign to End Loneliness and The Silver Line , a free and confidential call centre for people 55 and over . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Australia has the Coalition to End Loneliness . The U.S. has the doubled-barrelled Coalition to End Social Isolation and Loneliness . This year , the Dignity in Aging Act in the U.S. , which updates the 1965 Older Americans Act , put a major focus on social isolation and empowering local organizations to evaluate solutions for social isolation , incorporating social isolation screening into health and supportive services for seniors and creating a new focus on the issue of social isolation among older adults at the national level . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There is no other health condition that affects half of Americans , &amp;rdquo ; Andrew MacPherson , the director of the U.S. Coalition to End Social Isolation and Loneliness , told attendees at The Gerontological Society of America&amp;rsquo ; s annual scientific meeting last month . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Nobody saw this issue a year and a half ago , and we&amp;rsquo ; re already getting legislation in Washington . This is starting to get traction . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;7628;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;7670;TOOLONG ... is a potentially key way to combat loneliness -- but it 's difficult to get off the **27;7705;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Businesses are also responding to the issues of loneliness . One example is a &amp;ldquo ; concierge&amp;rdquo ; program that arranges rides from the ride-sharing service Lyft &lt;span class= " ILfuVd NA6bn " &gt;&lt;span class= " e24Kjd " &gt;for home-care clients who do n't have a smartphone or prefer to arrange their transportation by phone . **26;7734;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " ILfuVd NA6bn " &gt;&lt;span class= " e24Kjd " &gt; " **26;7762;TOOLONG The market is starting to react to the idea that loneliness is a condition that can be managed , &amp;rdquo ; said MacPherson. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While Canada doesn&amp;rsquo ; t have a national strategy , the issue is on the radar . The International Federation of Ageing report commissioned by Employment and Social Development Canada concluded that the top emerging issue facing seniors is keeping them socially connected and active . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last fall during the municipal election campaign , Ottawa Mayor Jim Watson promised an extra day of free transit for seniors . &amp;ldquo ; This measure is not only a cost-saving opportunity for seniors , it encourages them to leave their home and take part in social outings , helping to fight widespread loneliness and isolation affecting many seniors , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Everyone is looking for an answer about how to fix this , &amp;rdquo ; said Mary Pat Sullivan , a professor of social work and social gerontology at Nipissing University who recently returned to Canada from the U.K. , where she researched social isolation and loneliness for more than 20 years . &amp;ldquo ; I can see that interest is starting to pick up here . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The first &amp;ldquo ; summit on social isolation and companion animals&amp;rdquo ; was held in Washington last May , attracting public-health officials , gerontologists and veterinary researchers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Just last month , New York Times columnist Nicholas Kristof urged a war on loneliness and suggested it should be easier for people to have dogs because research has shown that dog owners&amp;nbsp ; &amp;mdash ; but not cat owners &amp;mdash ; are less lonely . ( Not exactly true . The growing body of research is mixed on whether pet ownership is a sure-fire balm for loneliness. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In October , menshealth.com posted an article arguing that men form friendships differently than women and need different ways to ward off loneliness . The headline ? &amp;ldquo ; Loneliness is fatal . Video games can keep men alive . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Free bus tickets , dogs and video games are only the start of the responses . Manitoba observes Let No One Be Alone Week , which encourages people to reach out to seniors . Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s Hey , Neighbour ! was a pilot project aimed at connecting apartment-dwellers through activities ranging from board game nights to an emergency preparedness workshop . The connections were organized by &amp;ldquo ; resident animators. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;7790;TOOLONG ... title= " R ? mi-Serge Gratton , front centre , and Ken Roberts , front right , belt it out at the " talent optional music jam " at the Centretown Community Health Centre . " alt= " R ? mi-Serge Gratton , front centre , and Ken Roberts , front right , belt it out at the " talent optional music jam " at the Centretown Community Health Centre . " data-portal-copyright= " JULIE OLIVER " **28;7826;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1516755 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Ontario , 11 community health centres , including the Centretown Community Health Centre , were part of a pilot project to issue &amp;ldquo ; social prescriptions&amp;rdquo ; for people who feel disconnected . The prescriptions were for activities ranging from dance lessons to museum visits to boost social connections . Doctors , nurses and other health professionals who identify social disconnectedness can refer clients to &amp;ldquo ; link workers&amp;rdquo ; who find social opportunities tailored to the client . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The project was based on similar strategies in the U.K. , where the National Health Service is fired up enough about social prescribing that it calls it a &amp;ldquo ; key component&amp;rdquo ; of universal personalized care . About 59 per cent of general practitioners think social prescribing can help reduce their workload . Last January , the NHS announced it was hiring 1,000 more link workers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ontario pilot project is wrapping up this month and a final report is due out in March , but a progress report noted that for some clients , spending time with others and socializing was a motivation for leaving home . One Ottawa client reported that a kinesiologist at the centre had suggested walking three times a week , but she found the motivation was greater after she joined a walking group . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We do better with others , &amp;rdquo ; said Natasha Beaudin , the Centretown Community Health Centre&amp;rsquo ; s project lead . Social prescribing has also helped to keep staff attuned to checking on loneliness in their interactions with clients . &amp;ldquo ; Living in downtown Ottawa can be pretty isolating , &amp;rdquo ; said Beaudin. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ken Roberts said activities like the talent optional music jam are a reason to leave his apartment . &amp;ldquo ; Unless I motivate myself , I just go to fortress mentality . I have to come up with strategies to motivate myself and interact with the world , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; R&amp;eacute ; mi-Serge Gratton , another member of the music jam , said it&amp;rsquo ; s important to feel like he&amp;rsquo ; s part of a community . Social prescribing is another way for people who are lonely to have an incentive to get out , he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When you&amp;rsquo ; re negative or depressed , your body has no resistance to anything else . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;7856;TOOLONG ... title= " The Centretown Community Health Centre has been part of a pilot project on " social prescribing " in which people who are identified as isolated are " prescribed " social activities , which can better overall well being and lower the health costs of isolation and loneliness . " alt= " The Centretown Community Health Centre has been part of a pilot project on " social prescribing " in which people who are identified as isolated are " prescribed " social activities , which can better overall well being and lower the health costs of isolation and loneliness . " data-portal-copyright= " JULIE OLIVER " **28;7892;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1518194 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Loneliness and social isolation might sound similar , but they are two different things . Social isolation is about the number and frequency of links in a person&amp;rsquo ; s social network . It is objective . Loneliness is a subjective thing &amp;mdash ; it&amp;rsquo ; s an individual reaction to the quality of those connections . It is possible to be socially isolated without being lonely . Two people may have completely different perceptions of the same social network . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You can have two people with the same network , and one person will be satisfied and the other will not , &amp;rdquo ; said Nancy Newall , an associate professor of psychology at Brandon University and loneliness researcher . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It has become increasingly clear that loneliness is a nuanced issue . The relationship between loneliness and health is a chicken-and-egg question . Loneliness can make people sick &amp;mdash ; people who are alone are less likely to take necessary medication , exercise or eat properly . Being sick can also contribute to loneliness . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Newall and fellow researcher Verena Menec have argued that the concepts of social isolation and loneliness should be considered together . Those who are &amp;ldquo ; lonely in a crowd&amp;rdquo ; may have a different health trajectory and benefit from different interventions than someone who is isolated and lonely , they concluded . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last June , the Angus Reid Institute released a study of social isolation in Canada , probing the number and frequency of social connections as well as the relative satisfaction with the quality of those connections . The study divided the respondents into five categories : the desolate ; lonely but not isolated ; isolated but not lonely ; moderately connected and cherished . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among the key findings : the cherished group &amp;mdash ; those who suffered from neither social isolation nor loneliness &amp;mdash ; are most likely to be married with children and higher incomes . Those 55-plus with incomes of less than $50,000 were twice as likely to be in the &amp;ldquo ; desolate&amp;rdquo ; group &amp;mdash ; they were both lonely and isolated , and were more than twice as likely as the cherished to be single and living alone . Almost a quarter of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s population fits into the desolate group , according to Angus Reid . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the U.K. , the focus on disconnectedness and its health effects went from being a grassroots movement to a national system in three years , said Sonia Hsiung , the lead on Ontario&amp;rsquo ; s social prescribing pilot projects . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Which is really speedy . I wonder if it&amp;rsquo ; s because everyone relates to it . Everyone likely has personal experience with social isolation , or they know someone who has . Social isolation resonates with everyone . I think it has captured the public&amp;rsquo ; s imagination . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In terms of a policy response to social isolation and loneliness , Hsiung doesn&amp;rsquo ; t think the Canadian health-care system is there yet &amp;mdash ; although she notes that the Ontario Health Teams , announced earlier this year by the province as a way to integrate and co-ordinate health care among agencies , are a good way to incorporate screening for loneliness and social isolation into heath care . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The momentum is growing , the need is growing , &amp;rdquo ; said Hsiung. &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re at the stage of planning how to build this into the health-care system . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;7922;TOOLONG ... title= " A physical health class for seniors has been part of the Centretown Community Health Centre 's repertoire for over a decade and , while it was n't intended as part of it 's recent initiative of " social prescribing , " such classes that bring people together have many great unintended consequences . " alt= " A physical health class for seniors has been part of the Centretown Community Health Centre 's repertoire for over a decade and , while it was n't intended as part of it 's recent initiative of " social prescribing , " such classes that bring people together have many great unintended consequences . " data-portal-copyright= " JULIE OLIVER " **28;7958;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1518195 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Angus Reid poll pointed out that it is possible to be lonely but not isolated . About 10 per cent of Canadians fit into this group . About four in 10 of these are under the age of 35 , and they score the highest in terms of having a university education . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another 15 per cent of Canadians felt isolated , but not lonely . Almost half of this group is 55 or older . Six out of 10 are married and almost half have children over 18 . Many are empty nesters. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The poll also found that 35 per cent of the &amp;ldquo ; lonely but not isolated&amp;rdquo ; group wished family and friends would spend more time visiting and socializing . Only two per cent of those who were &amp;ldquo ; isolated but not lonely&amp;rdquo ; said the same thing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The young are also more lonely than the elderly , surveys have repeatedly discovered . The BBC&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;ldquo ; loneliness experiment , &amp;rdquo ; an online survey that attracted 55,000 responses from around the world , found that 40 per cent of 16 to 24-year-old respondents said they often or very often feel lonely , compared with 27 per cent of those over 75 . Young people who took the survey reported higher levels of loneliness , no matter what their gender or country . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Should governments be in the business of alleviating loneliness ? There has been a bit of a &amp;ldquo ; moral panic&amp;rdquo ; around loneliness , said Christina Victor , a professor of gerontology and public health at Brunel University London . She feels that the coverage about loneliness in the U.K. has been alarmist , stigmatized the lonely and painted a picture of miserable older people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is also a lack of consensus about what should be done about loneliness &amp;mdash ; and some surprising findings about the experience of it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; About four-fifths of the respondents in the Angus Reid survey said they like spending time on their own . Only a third believe loneliness is about being on your own . People who said they were always alone were more likely to say they felt lonely . But those who live alone are only slightly more likely to feel lonely more often , the survey found . The finding suggests that living alone isn&amp;rsquo ; t as much of a problem as spending lots of time alone . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Victor&amp;nbsp ; is also skeptical about claims of adverse health outcomes linked to loneliness . A lot of studies that connect loneliness with poor health outcomes don&amp;rsquo ; t take into account other factors , such as widowhood . Disability and major life events , such as the loss of a spouse , can put older adults at risk of social isolation or loneliness . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Research has been flawed in terms of trying to untangle the causes and consequences , said Sullivan , the social work professor . &amp;ldquo ; Is loneliness worse than 15 cigarettes ? Why not 14 cigarettes ? It&amp;rsquo ; s an appealing headline , but we need more evidence . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although there have been links in the scientific literature between loneliness and conditions such as dementia , there is less evidence in the scientific literature on the effectiveness of interventions aimed at reducing loneliness , said Newall , the psychology professor . There is also a dispute over using terms like &amp;ldquo ; epidemic . &amp;rdquo ; It suggests loneliness is a contagious medical condition that can be contained . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Can loneliness be a good thing ? About 41 per cent of the respondents in the BBC project said there were positives . Nevertheless , they wanted to experience it a lot less . About 80 per cent had experienced loneliness at other points in their lives . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The experience may be very fleeting . It could last for a moment , a day or longer than that , &amp;rdquo ; said Sullivan . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Loneliness is not always bad , &amp;rdquo ; said Victor , who argues that there&amp;rsquo ; s a need for skepticism when it comes to claims that loneliness causes health conditions such as cognitive decline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;7988;TOOLONG ... title= " Loneliness is an issue around the world . " alt= " Loneliness is an issue around the world . " data-portal-copyright= " KatarzynaBialasiewicz " **28;8024;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1518229 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada has framed the discussion as &amp;ldquo ; social isolation&amp;rdquo ; rather than &amp;ldquo ; loneliness , &amp;rdquo ; said Sullivan . She believes this is a good thing . Loneliness is an experience that depends on the individual . Social isolation is a more neutral term , and from a research perspective , it is more quantifiable , she said . Framing it as social isolation normalizes the condition , and makes it a matter of social inclusion rather than turning loneliness into an &amp;ldquo ; older people&amp;rdquo ; problem . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sullivan doesn&amp;rsquo ; t think there&amp;rsquo ; s a need to appoint a minister of loneliness in Canada . &amp;ldquo ; They&amp;rsquo ; ve gone to the extreme in the U.K. But I see it shifting . They&amp;rsquo ; ve drawn attention to the fact that it&amp;rsquo ; s not a problem of old age . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Loneliness is a normal part of being human , said Newall. &amp;ldquo ; What we need to be concerned about is when it becomes chronic . It starts to really impact the way you see the world . If people experience failures in making and keeping friends , they start to withdraw , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s an emotion that all humans have . Loneliness is important , like all emotions . It tells us that something isn&amp;rsquo ; t right . That makes us aware that maybe we can change things . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sullivan agrees . She recalls a recent conversation with an Indigenous scholar who told her that &amp;ldquo ; loneliness is a teacher . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I stopped for a moment . And I thought : &amp;lsquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s teaching us that we need to get out , to reach out to friends or family , ' &amp;rdquo ; said Sullivan . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We may not be able to get rid of it because we&amp;rsquo ; re humans . We may not want to get rid of it because it may be a necessary experience . It may be the cue to an individual that they need to engage . Maybe we have to learn to be alone . Learn how to talk about it when we feel lonely , to minimize the pain . Or to embrace it sometimes . Introspection may be an opportunity . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Roberts still considers himself to be a work in progress . He has friends he feels are as close as family . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m at the point of my life where I have to start implementing changes or I face rapid decline , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; I have to resist the urge to think things aren&amp;rsquo ; t going to get better . It&amp;rsquo ; s easy to fall into morose , self-pitying despair . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;This article was written with the support of a journalism fellowship from The Gerontological Society of America , Journalists Network on Generations and the Silver Century Foundation . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;8054;TOOLONG ... title= " Ken Roberts . " alt= " Ken Roberts . " data-portal-copyright= " JULIE OLIVER " **28;8090;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1518198 " /&gt; Joanne LauciusThu , 19 Dec 2019 13:13:51 **45;8120;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; ChildLife StoryNationalSeniors'We can do better ' : City 's first health team to include community health centreshttp : **33;8167;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;8202;TOOLONG ... title= " Ontario Health Minister Christine Elliott " alt= " Ontario Health Minister Christine Elliott " data-portal-copyright= " Tijana Martin/The Canadian Press " **28;8238;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1365530 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A new model of health care delivery is set to begin in Ottawa with the announcement of the city&amp;rsquo ; s first health team . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ottawa Health Team &amp;mdash ; one of the groups designed to implement organizing and deliver health care in a new way &amp;mdash ; will get the green light from Health Minister Christine Elliott on Friday , this newspaper has learned . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Elliott , Ontario Minister of Health and Long Term Care , has begun announcing the first of what will initially be two dozen such health teams across the province in recent days . She was scheduled to make an announcement in Ottawa Friday morning . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eventually , the province plans to organize all health care into such teams , including hospitals , doctors , home care , clinics and other organizations . The teams are tasked with organizing patient care and smoothing transition for patients from different care providers and services . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The government originally said there could be up to 50 such teams around Ontario . But after receiving 150 applications from potential teams , Elliott conceded that there might eventually be more . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For now , 24 teams will be launched around the province as early adopters of the new system , including the Ottawa Health Team , which will include the region&amp;rsquo ; s major hospital , The Ottawa Hospital , as well as seven community health centres , Ottawa Public Health , Inner City Health , Bruy&amp;egrave ; re , and others . Among its aims are providing patient care and support in the most appropriate settings &amp;ldquo ; to achieve better outcomes and reduce costs . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The teams represent a key pillar of the Ford government&amp;rsquo ; s health restructuring agenda . But members of the public might not notice a huge change at first &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of the keys to the teams is that they will co-ordinate patient care . That means , for example , that patient information will be shared among partners in the team and patients will have help navigating the system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Elliott and others have used the example of easing patients&amp;rsquo ; transition from hospital to home care &amp;mdash ; something that can be disjointed and stressful under the current system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Through an Ontario Health Team , patients will experience easier transitions from one provider to another , including , for example , between hospitals and home care providers , with one patient story , one patient record and one care plan , &amp;rdquo ; Elliott said this week . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That co-ordination could take some time to be complete , though . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although the province has begun approving health teams under the new system , home care agencies still exist under the old system and are coordinated by ( local health integration networks ( known as LHINs ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ford government has announced that it plans to get rid of the LHINs &amp;mdash ; the system of 14 regional health coordinating bodies set up by the previous Liberal government &amp;mdash ; but that hasn&amp;rsquo ; t happened yet . So , for now , LHINs will continue to be in charge of home care . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eventually , home and community care functions will transfer to Ontario health teams , said Hayley Chazan , spokesperson for Elliott . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The ministry is planning carefully for these future changes and will have more information about timelines and funding models at a later date , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Officials with the Ottawa Health Team say they believe the various organizations working together can do a better job of keeping people healthy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We know that when people get sick and need health care , the current system is comprised of many silos , making it difficult for people to access care and navigate the transitions along the continuum of care , &amp;rdquo ; the Ottawa Health Team wrote in its submission to the province . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; By working together as a team , we believe we can do better at keeping people well and offering more seamless care when they need it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The health team is being led by the city&amp;rsquo ; s community health centres . Many health teams are led by hospitals , which are the biggest players . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ottawa Health Team was one of three local teams invited to submit full applications to become some of the first teams in the province . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; CHEO submitted an application to become a child-centred Kids First health team with an early focus on children with complex care and mental health needs and Montfort Hospital is part of a group that submitted an application to become a francophone focused health team . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is unclear whether more than one Ottawa team will be among the group of early approvals. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; epayne@postmedia.com &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;8268;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;8495;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1512824 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is an increasingly common story in Ontario &amp;mdash ; family members who say they are banned from visiting elderly loved ones after complaining about their institutional care . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Tuesday , Ottawa MPP Joel Harden asked the Minister of Seniors and Accessibility , Raymond Cho , to investigate the issue , saying some operators in the retirement home industry are engaging in &amp;ldquo ; questionable tactics . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Harden said some retirement homes are misusing trespassing laws to silence people who complain about care or services in the home . The regulatory body for retirement homes , he said , works at a &amp;ldquo ; glacial pace&amp;rdquo ; to respond to concerns . He said he would like to see the investigation extended to long-term care homes as well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This newspaper has reported on several cases of adult children who were banned from visiting their elderly parents in Ottawa long-term care homes after complaining about their care or conditions in the homes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Harden said he was concerned to hear about the case of Ottawa resident Mary Sardelis who was charged with trespassing after management of the retirement home where her mother lived called the police . Sardelis&amp;rsquo ; s case was documented on the CBC program Marketplace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sardelis said s &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;he was prevented from seeing her 97-year-old mother for most of the past year until the charged was withdrawn last month . She was allowed in last Dec. 23 to quickly deliver a gift to her mother . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The home&amp;rsquo ; s owners , who claim police were called because Sardelis was being abusive and disruptive to staff , say she could have come back at any time if she signed an agreement . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But Sardelis , who is now being sued by the retirement home for defamation , said the agreement was essentially a &amp;ldquo ; gag order&amp;rdquo ; that would have limited her visits with her mother to one hour in the evening and prevented her from ever criticizing the retirement home . She is back visiting her mother again , but said she feels like her every move is being watched . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sardelis said the investigative body for retirement homes , the Retirement Homes Regulatory Authority , investigated and found no evidence of the retirement home&amp;rsquo ; s allegations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She said it is &amp;ldquo ; about time&amp;rdquo ; there was an investigation into the use of trespass law to keep people from visiting loved ones . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This is long overdue . People are saying thanks for bringing awareness ( to this issue ) . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Keith McLaren , lawyer for the retirement home where Sardelis&amp;rsquo ; s mother lives , said it is not illegal for retirement residences to issue trespass notices . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; McLaren added that the home , as part of the defamation lawsuit against her and nine other people , is asking that Sardelis be permanently banned from visiting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sardelis&amp;rsquo ; s lawyer Mitchell Rowe said the defamation suit is aimed at Sardelis and a group of people who picketed the retirement home , for which they had a permit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Advocates for the elderly say the issue is increasingly common and worrisome. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Living in a long-term care home can be a lonely and isolating experience , cut off from the outside world . One of the most important ways that a resident&amp;rsquo ; s day can be brightened up is by having a visitor . Unfortunately , residents may encounter issues in having visitors , and visitors may encounter problems when attempting to visit residents , &amp;rdquo ; wrote Jane Meadus , lawyer for the Advocacy Centre for the Elderly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2017 , two local women were issued no trespass notices and told to leave the long-term care homes in Ottawa where their mothers lived , in separate incidents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Both of the women , who are retired hospital nurses , said the homes were using no trespass notices and threats of fines to gag them after they complained about substandard care . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You complain and this is the price you pay , &amp;rdquo ; said one woman whose mother is disabled . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Advocates say trespass laws are being abused to keep people who complain out of institutions that care for seniors . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A spokesperson for Seniors Minister Raymond Cho noted that the provincial government regulates but does not fund the retirement home sector . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Retirement Homes Regulatory Authority administers the Retirement Homes Act on behalf of the government . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If family members of residents are concerned about conditions in retirement homes please contact the Retirement Homes Regulatory Authority at 1-855-275-7472 or at info@rhra.ca , &amp;rdquo ; said director of communications Pooja Parekh. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;8525;TOOLONG ... NewsSeniorsProposed Ontario drug regulation changes worry policy expertshttp : **33;8677;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;8712;TOOLONG ... title= " A 2016 file photo of Dr. Joel Lexchin. " alt= " A 2016 file photo of Dr. Joel Lexchin. " data-portal-copyright= " Tyler Anderson/Naitonal Post " **28;8748;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1509861 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ontario government is proposing drug regulation changes that it says will remove red tape and barriers for pharmaceutical companies , allowing some drugs to bypass the normal approval process during a shortage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;8778;TOOLONG ... shortages , including the often-used breast cancer drug tamoxifen&lt;/a&gt; , have been wide-spread and increasing in recent years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The move , the government says , would allow alternative drug products to quickly enter the market during a shortage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , the move is being met with resistance by some drug policy experts who say more information is needed to ensure the changes are good for consumers &amp;mdash ; and whether the changes will actually help prevent long-term drug shortages . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The changes , part of the government&amp;rsquo ; s larger push to reduce red tape , would also make it easier for companies to raise or lower drug prices in other cases , depending on the market . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a document about the proposed changes , the government says they would ensure that Ontario remains &amp;ldquo ; open for business&amp;rdquo ; for the pharmacy and pharmaceutical industry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The proposals , called &amp;ldquo ; Reducing Administrative Burden to Drug Manufacturers and Pharmacies , &amp;rdquo ; are part of an omnibus red tape reduction bill that was introduced at the end of October while the legislature was recessed . They affect prescription drugs , mainly generics. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some drug policy experts fear the changes would remove some consumer protections , are being introduced with little publicity and will do little to address long-term drug shortages . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pharmaceutical policy expert Dr. Joel Lexchin , who teaches at York University&amp;rsquo ; s School of Health Policy and Management , said he is concerned about the lack of consultation and transparency around the changes . Some of the proposals respond to requests from the pharmaceutical industry with apparently little or no input from consumers or healthcare providers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; More details are needed , he said , before the changes go ahead . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It should not be the job of the Ontario Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care to advocate on behalf of the pharmaceutical industry . The job of the Ministry of Health should be the protection of the health of Ontarians , &amp;rdquo ; wrote Lexchin in a submission to the Ministry of Health . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Before the ministry goes ahead with these changes it needs to provide much more information and show that these changes will put the health of the people of Ontario above the interests of the commercial entities that are advocating for them . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jacalyn Duffin , professor emerita and Hannah Chair of the History of Medicine at Queen&amp;rsquo ; s University , said she only learned about the proposals when a law firm blogged about them . She said she finds some of them shocking . &amp;ldquo ; They will remove some consumer protections and probably will not help the shortages . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The proposed changes include an amendment that would make it easier for generic drug companies to adjust their prices if the number of competitors on the market changes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Under the current model , generic drugs are priced at a percentage of the brand price , depending on how many competitors there are . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For example , if a brand label drug costs $10 , generic makers could charge $7.50 or $8 , but that price would decrease based on the number of competitors . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The proposed changes allow drug companies to more easily adjust their prices when competitors come in and out of the market , something the government says should reduce the price of generic drugs . However , it could also allow companies to increase the price of generics , especially at a time of consolidations of drug companies and shortages . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Justin Bates , Chief Executive Officer of the Ontario Pharmacists Association , said the change enables Ontario pharmacies to operate on a level playing field with pharmacies in every other province , except Quebec . Ordinary commercial terms are a normal part of business , he said , and do not increase drug costs , which are regulated by a Canada-wide system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The proposed changes would also exempt certain drugs from drug submission requirements , allowing quicker funding of a drug that could fill in during a shortage . Funding of the alternative drug would be temporary , the government says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A spokesman for Health Minister Christine Elliott dismissed concerns that the changes had been brought in quietly and with too little information , saying they were part of a &amp;ldquo ; high-profile&amp;rdquo ; government wide announcement of red tape reduction proposals and will help the government respond to patient needs in the event of potential drug shortages . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The proposed changes would allow an alternative drug product to be temporarily funded under the Ontario Drug Benefit program during a supply interruption that may be due to a drug shortage &amp;hellip ; and is expected to lead to significant patient risk or harm , &amp;rdquo ; said Hayley Chazan , a spokesperson for Health Minister Christine Elliott . &amp;ldquo ; This proposal , if approved , would mitigate supply gaps of funded products for recipients of the Ontario Drug Benefit program . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But Lexchin said the proposed changes are simply reactive and lack any proactive measures to deal with future drug shortages . New Zealand , for example , requires drug companies to guarantee there will be sufficient supply before approving the drug for the health system . If the company runs out of drugs , it is then their responsibility to source a replacement , not the government&amp;rsquo ; s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Paul Grootendorst , associate professor in the Faculty of Pharmacy at the University of Toronto said the proposed changes allowing generic companies to change their prices up or down when the number of competitors changes make sense . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t see any problems , &amp;rdquo ; he said of the proposals . &amp;ldquo ; These are more housekeeping issues . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The government is seeking comment on the proposals until Nov. 27. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; epayne@postmedia.com &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;8813;TOOLONG ... bodies are piling up ' : Inside the opioid epidemic and the crisis that wo n't go away&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;8848;TOOLONG ... concerned they ca n't provide proper care in crowded hospitals , says union&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;8883;TOOLONG ... was bawling ' : Injured Bronco 's mother stunned by his progress after surgery&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Elizabeth PayneFri , 22 Nov 2019 11:39:55 **45;8918;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; ChildLocal NewsSeniorsWomenU.S. stem cell clinic offering unapproved therapies brings direct-to-consumer marketing to Ottawahttp : **34;8965;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;9001;TOOLONG ... title= " A doctor a private U.S. clinic injects a patient with stem cells to treat cartilage wastage joint injury and pain . " alt= " A doctor a private U.S. clinic injects a patient with stem cells to treat cartilage wastage joint injury and pain . " data-portal-copyright= " edward olive " **28;9037;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1507409 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Just a few months after Health Canada began cracking down on private clinics offering unapproved stem cell therapies , at least one U.S. clinic has moved in to fill the vacuum with direct marketing to Canadian consumers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The clinic from Burlington , Vermont , even offers shuttle buses to transport people from Ottawa to the clinic four hours away for treatment it suggests will end joint pain , among other things . Lunch and dinner are free , but each injection costs $6,880 . Two for $10,880. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The treatments , using umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells , are not approved in either Canada or the United States . Health Canada warns that Canadians who travel abroad for stem cell treatments &amp;ldquo ; may put themselves at risk . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While stem cells , which were discovered at the University of Toronto in 1961 by James Till and Ernest McCulloch , promise to revolutionize many treatments and could offer breakthroughs for diseases , almost all are still considered experimental and have yet to be proven safe or effective . Clinical trials on numerous potential stem cell therapies are under way , including in Ottawa . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While research progresses , private stem cell clinics have popped up around the world making promises for treatments not yet proven safe or effective . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A 2018 study by Leigh Turner of the University of Minnesota Center for Bioethics found 43 clinics offering stem cell treatments in Canada and 750 in the U.S. Earlier this year , Health Canada sent Canadian clinics , including some in Ottawa , cease-and-desist letters . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Clinics in Vermont , near the Canadian border , appear to have ramped up marketing to Canadians since then . One clinic has been holding back-to-back seminars . Another says it stopped marketing in Canada after receiving a warning from Health Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There have been cases of harm as a result of treatments , including two women who had permanent damage to their sight after stem cells were injected into their eyes at a Florida clinic . Other patients have been infected with unsterilized equipment and others have developed tumours at the site of stem cell injections. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A common harm , critics say , is exploitation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;9067;TOOLONG ... title= " Dr. Michael Rudnicki is director of the regenerative medicine program and Sprott Centre for Stem Cell Research at the Ottawa Hospital Research Institute , says of stem cell therapy claims : ' If it sounds too good to be true , it probably is too good to be true . ' " alt= " Dr. Michael Rudnicki is director of the regenerative medicine program and Sprott Centre for Stem Cell Research at the Ottawa Hospital Research Institute , says of stem cell therapy claims : ' If it sounds too good to be true , it probably is too good to be true . ' " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;9103;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1507406 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Health officials say the clinics are misusing the promise of stem cell therapy to exploit vulnerable patients . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; These patients are in pain and they are suffering and they are looking for help and they are being exploited , &amp;rdquo ; said Dr. Michael Rudnicki , director of the regenerative medicine program and Sprott Centre for Stem Cell Research at the Ottawa Hospital Research Institute . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If it sounds too good to be true , it probably is too good to be true . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At a recent seminar at a west-end Ottawa hotel meeting room , Roseanna Ammendolea of the Vermont Center for Regenerative Medicine told a packed room that her clinic and others like it had successfully treated people for pain related to arthritis , neuropathy and other ailments that affected joints using mesenchymal stem cells from umbilical cords . The stem cells , she claimed , are both effective and safe , saying there had been no issues with cell rejection . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We will not give injections if we feel that this injection will not be beneficial to our patients . This is why we are so successful . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Participants , including some who walked with canes and others who talked about being in pain and having mobility issues , were shown videos of people described as Canadian clients who claimed the treatments worked . One man said it was &amp;ldquo ; probably the best money I have spent in my life as far as my health . &amp;rdquo ; Another said she would do it again &amp;ldquo ; in a heartbeat&amp;rdquo ; and was able to do things she hadn&amp;rsquo ; t been able to do earlier . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They were also shown a slide showing long wait times for hip and knee replacements in Ontario , &amp;ldquo ; We are not a priority , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; Where does that leave us ? &amp;rdquo ; Participants weren&amp;rsquo ; t told exactly how the stem cells were supposed to work , but claimed they had successfully improved pain and mobility issues in clients . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What the seminar goers weren&amp;rsquo ; t told is that , even in the U.S. , the treatment is not covered by health insurance because it remains unproven. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The U.S. Federal Drug Administration has issued a warning to consumers not to use cell therapies that are unapproved or unproven. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Stem cells have been called everything from cure-alls to miracle treatments . But don&amp;rsquo ; t believe the hype . Some unscrupulous providers offer stem cell products that are both unapproved and unproven . So beware of potentially dangerous procedures &amp;mdash ; and confirm what&amp;rsquo ; s really being offered before you consider &lt;em&gt;any&lt;/em&gt; &amp;nbsp ; treatment , &amp;rdquo ; the FDA said in a statement . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The only stem-cell-based products that are FDA-approved for use in the United States are blood-forming stem cells derived from cord blood&amp;nbsp ; for limited use in patients with disorders affecting the body system that is involved in the production of blood . Bone marrow is also used for these treatments , but is generally not regulated by the FDA for that use . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Health Canada has granted market authorization for a stem cell therapy to treat graft-versus-host disease and two cell-based gene therapies to treat certain cancers . Most cell therapies are still experimental . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I totally understand the skepticism of it , &amp;rdquo ; Doug Argento , who works at the Vermont Center for Regenerative Medicine , said in a telephone interview , &amp;ldquo ; but the fact is that things that are approved now and medically paid for were seen as renegade 20 or 30 years ago . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The treatment employs technology developed by Neil Riordan , founder , chairman and chief science officer of the Stem Cell Institute in Panama , using human umbilical cord tissue-derived mesenchymal stem cells . There are 41 such clinics across the U.S. Riordan also played a role in the development of a nutritional product called Stem-Kine , which producers claim &amp;mdash ; without scientific backing &amp;mdash ; increases the number of stem cells circulating in a person&amp;rsquo ; s body . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The stem cells injected in the clinic , Argento said , are from umbilical cord tissue as a result of caesarean births to reduce risk of infection . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rudnicki , of The Ottawa Hospital Research Institute , says there is &amp;ldquo ; no evidence that these sorts of cells are regenerative at all . It would not pass muster in Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The public has to understand that there are people out to remove them from their money . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rudnicki says he regularly receives inquiries from people desperate to get stem cell treatments . He says he tries to connect them with clinical trials that they might be able to participate in. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rudnicki noted there were multiple clinical trials in Canada , including treatments of autoimmune diseases , trials involving treatment for Type 1 diabetes and others . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; But the use of these inappropriate cell types for treating arthritis and joints and so on is certainly not approved by Health Canada and would not be allowed in Canada under the regulations . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is some evidence that injections of some stem cell products might have a temporary positive impact on inflammation , he said , but it will not be regenerative and will not restore function to joints . &amp;ldquo ; They are being sold a bill of goods . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Leigh Turner of the University of Minnesota Center for Bioethics , meanwhile , says the explosion in clinics offering unproven stem cell therapies in the U.S. is &amp;ldquo ; a marketplace that traffics in misrepresentation . It is easy to see how people are taken advantage of and scammed. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is also difficult to find out about physical harms being done to patients . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There are no safety studies . We don&amp;rsquo ; t have good data . But we do know there have been some serious harms. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Stem cell therapies have the potential to become standard treatment in some areas , but they are not there yet , Turner said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Businesses are tapping into genuine human suffering , desperation and also hope . &amp;ldquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Turner also noted there was an &amp;ldquo ; excellent chance&amp;rdquo ; that the vials of liquid being injected into patients did not actually contain stem cells . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dr. Jonathan Fenton of another stem cell clinic in Burlington , the Vermont Regenerative Medicine , said he had complained about the new clinic , the Vermont Center for Regenerative Medicine , which has a similar name and employs hard-sell tactics , he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His clinic takes bone marrow from patients&amp;rsquo ; hips and injects it . The procedure is done the same day . He says he regularly sees Canadian patients for bone marrow aspiration therapy and platelet-rich plasma treatments , using their own blood . The treatments , he says , speed healing and are allowed in the U.S. The use of bone marrow aspiration is neither proven nor allowed in Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fenton , who is secretary-treasurer of the American Academy of Orthopedic Medicine , acknowledged many people offering stem cell treatments are &amp;ldquo ; not doing it to the highest ethical standards . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He has filed complaints with state officials over clinics selling unsafe or fraudulent treatments . &amp;ldquo ; I have asked the state and federal judiciary to close down this clinic for committing fraud . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He said his platelet and bone marrow treatments were covered by a major Vermont health insurer because they saw the cost of benefits were going down and patients were requiring fewer surgeries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He said he was told by Health Canada that he could not market in Canada . Representatives of the Vermont Center for Regenerative Medicine , meanwhile , said they had discussions with Health Canada about what they could and could not say when marketing in Canada before holding seminars in Ottawa and Halifax . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We have looked at the information provided and have not identified any immediate non-compliance with advertising regulations pertaining to Canadian health products , &amp;rdquo ; a Health Canada spokesperson said , adding that the agency was continuing to assess . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Back at a west-end Ottawa hotel , some participants in the seminar , including a retired pharmacist , said they were considering getting the treatments . &amp;ldquo ; But it&amp;rsquo ; s expensive . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another participant said he was skeptical. &amp;ldquo ; They seemed very sketchy when I went online . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **27;9133;TOOLONG " **34;9162;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;9198;TOOLONG ... and Kaushic : We 're losing the fight against superbugs&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;9233;TOOLONG ... who live to at least 110 , boast stronger immune systems , helping them fight off diseases&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;9268;TOOLONG ... stimulator ' really promising ' : Survivor moves legs for first time since Humboldt bus crash&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Elizabeth PayneMon , 18 Nov 2019 11:51:22 **45;9303;TOOLONG ... **27;9350;TOOLONG century of trauma : Tracing the evolution of PTSD through four soldiershttp : **32;9379;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;9413;TOOLONG ... title= " Pte . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;9449;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1500695 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; On the opening morning of the Battle of Vimy Ridge , Capt . Thain MacDowell ran towards enemy lines through a welter of mud and craters , sleet and machine gunfire . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He reached his objective , a German trench , only to find that he had become separated from most of his company . Joined by a pair of army couriers , MacDowell captured two machine gun placements , then climbed down a flight of steps into a deep dugout . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Around a sharp corner , he confronted a roomful of German soldiers . He turned and shouted to an imaginary group of Canadians behind him to hold their grenades . Seventy-seven Germans surrendered . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;9479;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;9521;TOOLONG ...
